title: Not Feeling Well
subtitle: かぜ・ずつう・ぎっくりごし
review: Written by Claude. The Japanese, the romaji and the humor have not been checked by a Japanese speaker. English support only: no Burmese lines yet.
intro: A slight fever that will not stop a man from going to the office, a headache and grandmother's cures, a back thrown out by a sneeze, and an appetite that comes back for ramen only: four short scenes between Emi and Riku. Listen for ga itai when something hurts, for the advice with hō ga ii, and for how you say you feel a little better.

lines.kana: エミ、ちょっとぐあいがわるい。
lines.say: エミ、ちょっと具合が悪い。

tr.en: Emi, I don't feel so good.

lines.note: Guai ga warui: to feel unwell. Chotto, a little, makes it softer.
The everyday question when someone looks unwell or upset.

lines.romaji: Nodo ga itai. Hanamizu mo deru. Seki mo deru.
lines.kana: のどがいたい。はなみずもでる。せきもでる。
lines.say: 喉が痛い。鼻水も出る。咳も出る。

tr.en: My throat hurts. My nose is running. And I'm coughing.

lines.note: Part of the body + ga itai: it hurts. Hanamizu ga deru, seki ga deru: a runny nose, a cough come out. Mo: also.
Netsu: fever. Netsu ga aru: to have a fever.

lines.kana: さんじゅうななどにぶ。
lines.note: Body temperature is said in do (degrees) and bu (tenths): 37.2 = sanjūnana-do ni-bu.
Binetsu: a slight fever. In Japan people take 37 and a bit seriously.

lines.kana: びねつ…もうだめかもしれない。
lines.say: 微熱…もうだめかもしれない。

tr.en: A slight fever… I may not make it.

lines.note: Mō dame: it's all over. Kamo shirenai: maybe.

tr.en: Are you taking the day off work?

lines.note: Kaisha: the company, the office. Yasumu: to rest, to take time off.
Iya: a casual no. Iku: to go.
Genki: well, healthy. Jan is casual: see, you are!
Atama: head. The noun for a headache is zutsū.
Itsu: when. Kara: from, since.
Kesa: this morning.
Kusuri o nomu: to take medicine. Japanese says drink, even for a pill.

lines.romaji: Obāchan ga itteta. Kubi ni negi o maku to ii tte.
lines.kana: おばあちゃんがいってた。くびにねぎをまくといいって。
lines.say: おばあちゃんが言ってた。首にネギを巻くといいって。

tr.en: Grandma used to say: wrap a leek around your neck.

lines.note: An old home cure for a cold. …to ii: it is good to… Tte: she said that.
Kaze: a cold. Desho: isn't it? She knows the cure, and it is the wrong one.

lines.romaji: Jā, umeboshi o odeko ni haru.
lines.kana: じゃあ、うめぼしをおでこにはる。
lines.say: じゃあ、梅干しをおでこに貼る。

tr.en: Then stick a pickled plum on your forehead.

lines.note: Umeboshi: a salty pickled plum. Odeko: forehead. Haru: to stick on. Another old cure, this one for headaches.
Ne: she is telling him what she has decided.

tr.en: Shall I go and buy a leek?

lines.note: Katte kuru: go, buy and come back.

lines.romaji: Shizuka ni shite kuretara, naoru to omou.
lines.kana: しずかにしてくれたら、なおるとおもう。
lines.say: 静かにしてくれたら、治ると思う。

tr.en: If you'd be quiet, I think it would go away.

lines.note: Shizuka ni suru: to be quiet. …te kuretara: if you did that for me. Naoru: to get better. To omou: I think.
Ita!: ow! Koshi: the lower back. Gikkuri-goshi is a back that suddenly gives out.
Ugoku: to move. Ugokenai: can't move.
Kushami: a sneeze. A sneeze really is a classic cause of gikkuri-goshi.
De: because of, by.

lines.kana: おおきいくしゃみだった。
lines.say: 大きいくしゃみだった。
lines.note: Ōkii: big. Datta: was.

lines.romaji: Byōin ni itta hō ga ii yo.
lines.kana: びょういんにいったほうがいいよ。
lines.say: 病院に行ったほうがいいよ。

tr.en: You should go and see a doctor.

lines.note: Past form + hō ga ii: you should. Byōin: hospital or clinic, the place you go to see a doctor.
Aruku: to walk. Arukeru: can walk.
Arukenai: can't walk.

lines.romaji: Jā, kyō wa soko de nete ne. Oyasumi.
lines.kana: じゃあ、きょうはそこでねてね。おやすみ。
lines.say: じゃあ、今日はそこで寝てね。おやすみ。

tr.en: Then sleep there tonight. Good night.

lines.note: Soko de: there, where you are. Nete ne: sleep, will you.
The question to ask someone who is ill.

lines.romaji: Sukoshi yoku natta. Demo, mada shokuyoku ga nai.
lines.kana: すこしよくなった。でも、まだしょくよくがない。
lines.say: 少しよくなった。でも、まだ食欲がない。

tr.en: A little better. But I still have no appetite.

lines.note: Yoku naru: to get better. Shokuyoku: appetite. Mada… nai: still not.
Okayu: soft rice porridge, what you eat in Japan when you are ill.

lines.kana: ありがとう。…ラーメンがたべたい。
lines.say: ありがとう。…ラーメンが食べたい。
lines.note: Verb stem + tai: want to. Taberu, tabetai.

lines.kana: しょくよく、あるじゃん。

tr.en: So you do have an appetite.

lines.note: Aru jan: see, you have one.

tr.en: Ramen goes in a separate stomach.

lines.note: Betsubara: the separate stomach. Usually said about dessert when you are already full.

lines.kana: いちにちさんかい、しょくごに。

tr.en: Three times a day, after meals.

lines.note: Ichinichi sankai: three times a day. Shokugo: after a meal. What is written on the medicine bag.

lines.romaji: Jā, genki da ne. Ashita wa kaisha da yo.
lines.kana: じゃあ、げんきだね。あしたはかいしゃだよ。
lines.say: じゃあ、元気だね。明日は会社だよ。

tr.en: Then you're well. You have work tomorrow.

lines.romaji: … Yappari, mada netsu ga aru kamo.
lines.kana: …やっぱり、まだねつがあるかも。
lines.say: …やっぱり、まだ熱があるかも。

tr.en: …Actually, I may still have a fever.

lines.note: Yappari: on second thought. Kamo: short for kamo shirenai, maybe.

notes: Pain: part of the body + ga itai. Atama ga itai (head), nodo ga itai (throat), koshi ga itai (lower back), onaka ga itai (stomach).
Feeling: guai ga warui (I feel unwell), sukoshi yoku natta (I'm a little better), genki (well).
A cold: kaze. Netsu ga aru (I have a fever), seki ga deru (I'm coughing), hanamizu ga deru (my nose is running).
Temperature: 37.2 is sanjūnana-do ni-bu. A slight fever is binetsu.
Advice: past form + hō ga ii. Byōin ni itta hō ga ii: you should see a doctor.
Medicine is drunk: kusuri o nomu. Ichinichi sankai, shokugo ni: three times a day, after meals.
Can and can't: arukeru, arukenai (walk); ugokeru, ugokenai (move).

questions.q: Riku's temperature is 37.2. What does Emi call it?
questions.why: Binetsu: a slight fever. He is going to work anyway.

questions.q: Emi has a headache. How does she say it?
questions.why: Atama: head. Nodo: throat. Koshi: lower back.

questions.q: What does Emi think will cure her headache?
options: A pickled plum on her forehead
questions.why: Shizuka ni shite kuretara, naoru to omou.

questions.q: How did Riku hurt his back?
questions.why: Kushami: a sneeze. Ōkii kushami datta.

questions.q: Riku has no appetite. What does he want to eat?
questions.why: Rāmen ga tabetai. Rāmen wa betsubara.
